newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Polls open in Chechen elections.
newsitem.headline: Polls open in Chechen elections.

text.p: Chechens began voting on Monday in presidential and parliamentary elections which many hope will reinforce their demands that Russia must grant sovereignty to the mainly Moslem region.
Voters trickled into polling stations in the war-shattered capital Grozny shortly after they opened at 7 a.m. (0400 GMT).
International observers from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) were on hand in one station to watch ballot boxes being assembled.
Aslan Maskhadov, who led rebel Chechen fighters in a two-year guerrilla war against Russian forces, was the clear frontrunner to win the presidential race.

But all the main candidates in the 13-man field have committed themselves to turning the de facto autonomy secured by last month's withdrawal of Russian troops into full sovereignty after 200 years of deeply unpopular Russian rule.
Russia, fearing instability on its volatile southern flank and unrest among other ethnic minorities, flatly opposes secession.
